thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: unusual auth traffic pattern detected on /v1/generate. 401s followed by retries, spike +240% vs baseline. Suggested severity: P2. Please ack and triage.

alex_w: ack. jumping in. seeing concentrated traffic from a handful of IPs, mixed 401 then retries that sometimes succeed. attaching quick grep output in a sec.

maria_s: @alex_w can you paste a few sample auth log lines? need to know key ids and user-agent patterns. could be credential stuffing or a leaked service credential.

alex_w: sample logs pasted below:

```
2026-03-15T02:12:07Z auth-proxy req=rx1 client_ip=54.23.11.8 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=401 auth_method=service_key key_id=svc-prod-42 ua="curl/7.68.0"
2026-03-15T02:12:07Z auth-proxy req=rx2 client_ip=54.23.11.8 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 upstream=runtime1 latency_ms=28 auth_method=service_key key_id=svc-prod-42
```

alex_w: lots of retries from same IPs, varying UAs. suspicious.

sec-eng-lee: stepping in. pattern consistent with a leaked key being exercised + some partial caching causing occasional successes. start S3 artifact audit for anything with env/credentials in name or build artifacts.

jordan_oncall: oncall taking lead. @maria_s you'll coordinate sec actions. @cs-amy please flag customer ops in case any customer endpoints saw instability.

maria_s: starting S3 search for last 72h for keys: filenames containing env, .env, secrets, credentials, deploy/config. will report matches.

infra-bot: proposed WAF mitigation: block IPs with >100 auth fails in 10m window. candidate CIDR 54.23.11.0/24.

jordan_oncall: do NOT block broadly yet. prefer graduated controls: apply rate-limit + challenge first. full block only if malicious traffic persists after mitigation.

alex_w: applied temporary rate-limit profile "suspicious-auth-temp" -> 60r/s per IP and 429 after burst. monitoring auth failure trend now.

maria_s: S3 audit result: found artifact uploaded by internal-ci containing deploy/.env.debug with an entry referencing svc-prod-42. upload time 2026-03-14T22:03:11Z. ACL was private but file appears to have been mirrored to a public cache via our CI mirror job.

cs-amy: FYI two Dedicated customers reported transient failures ~02:15 UTC. CS investigating if any requests from those customers correlate to the suspicious key usage.

jordan_oncall: immediate actions we need:
- create replacement key(s) for svc-prod account
- roll keys to canaries (small subset of services) then prod
- temporarily throttle/challenge suspicious traffic at edge
- notify customers with a precautionary notice
- preserve logs and evidence for forensic review

maria_s: drafting rotation commands. example (IAM):
```
# mark old access key inactive
aws iam update-access-key --user-name svc-prod --access-key-id KEYID-OLD --status Inactive
# create new access key and push to Vault
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-prod
```

alex_w: caution: we must identify all consumers of KEYID-OLD first. I'll run greps and auth log queries to list services referencing it. can't disable until canaries hardened.

maria_s: agree. plan: mark old key Inactive (not deleted) -> deploy new key to canaries -> monitor 30m -> if stable, deactivate across remaining services -> after 1h revoke old key.

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call rotation in 45m. please prepare handoff notes.

jordan_oncall: @ops-bot schedule handoff to night-oncall @matt at 03:30 UTC. Handoff summary: possible leaked service key svc-prod-42 found in CI artifact; edge rate-limits live; key rotation in progress; CS notified.

matt (night-oncall): acking pre-handoff. please ensure runbook includes exact commands, where to find consumer list, and incident tracker link.

alex_w: runbook snippets:
```
# find references
rg "svc-prod-42" -S /repos /deploy /etc -g '!node_modules' || true
# auth log query
jq -r '. | select(.key_id=="svc-prod-42") | [.ts, .service, .ip] | @tsv' /var/log/auth-proxy/*.json | tail -200
```

maria_s: short rotation checklist:
1) create new key pair and store in Vault (tag svc-prod/v2)
2) update canary services (5% traffic) and validate
3) monitor error/latency for 15-30m
4) mark old key inactive
5) revoke old key after 60m of stability
6) cleanup S3 artifact and harden CI publishing pipeline

cs-amy: customer message draft:
"We detected abnormal traffic tied to an internal CI credential. We have applied temporary rate-limiting and rotated the credential. We're investigating whether any customer-specific data was exposed; we'll notify affected customers directly if any exposure is confirmed."

jordan_oncall: send to the two impacted customers with legal cc. mark severity customer-impact P2.

maria_s: opened infra repo issue to remove artifact and patch CI: https://git.redwood/infra/cleanup/456 (internal). also scheduled a deletion of the mirrored public cache.

infra-bot: mitigation applied: edge profile "suspicious-auth-temp" active -> 60r/s + challenge on retries.

alex_w: metrics update: auth failures down ~80% since rate-limit applied. still seeing a handful of successful calls using old key from three internal hosts (likely internal jobs).

maria_s: rolling new key to canaries now. will monitor health checks.

~30m later

maria_s: canary rollout stable. created new key and pushed to Vault as "svc-prod/key v2".

jordan_oncall: proceed to mark old key Inactive. keep it inactive for 1h then revoke if no regressions.

maria_s: old key KEYID-OLD marked Inactive at 03:05 UTC. distributing revocation notes.

incident-bot: update: customer impact: two enterprise customers saw short transient errors (2-3 minutes). no evidence of customer data exfiltration so far. severity remains P2 pending S3 artifact audit and mirror purge.

cs-amy: customer notifications sent and flagged for follow-up calls. legal engaged as precaution.

matt (night-oncall): taking over monitoring now for the 60m window. checklist run: verified edge profile active, old key Inactive, Vault v2 entry present, CS/legal notified. will escalate on any uptick.

jordan_oncall: handing off complete. incident tracker: https://incident-board/redwood/INC-2026-0315-09. leaving notes: root cause likely CI artifact with a service key; mitigations: rate-limit/challenge, canary rotation, artifact cleanup. postmortem required.

maria_s: follow-ups assigned: audit all buckets for similar artifact names, rotate any additional keys found in artifact, add CI artifact secret scanning and blocklist for filenames, tighten mirror publish ACLs.

incident-bot: status -> monitoring. assigned: maria_s, alex_w, matt. next update in 60m or on major change.

matt (night-oncall): acknowledged. starting 60m monitor. will confirm final revocation and mirror purge when done.
